_about: Track U's interface data (scripts/ui/: unit markers, the roster sidebar, the motion planner and its orders card). EVERY VALUE HERE IS PROPOSED by Track U on 2026-10-09 so the demo has an interface; none is a decision until Alex makes one (data/decisions/decisions.json). Read by scripts/ui/ui_style.gd: a key the code asks for and this file does not hold is an error at load, never a default in code.
_colours: Colours are ROLES, never hexes (working rule 6, docs/proposals/palette-architecture.md). A role is {base, shade?, toward?, t?, alpha?}: base is a colour of data/params/render_defaults.json -- paper, ink, object_fill, wall_fill, rock_fill, roof_lit, dirt, shadow (the chosen shadow tint), side_a, side_b; shade names one of the palette's own shadow-mix fractions (roof_shaded_shadow_mix, wall_slope_shadow_mix) and mixes the shadow tint in by it, rounded to 8 bits as the prototype's mix() does; toward + t mixes toward another palette colour; alpha is a number or the name of a render parameter (shadow_strength). Hue stays reserved for paper, ink, shadow and the side accents.

sides._reason: World units carry a side name; the palette has two accents (Alex 2026-10-09: side_a brick red, side_b slate blue, 'might be useful colours to mirror in the HUD'). The players' side takes side_a, as on the unit sheet's default view.

unit_art._reason: The unit sheet's plane generators (reference/mockups/unit_sheet.html genPlane/buildPlane/drawPlane), ported to scripts/ui/unit_marker_art.gd. variant is the sheet's variant letter as an index (0 = a, the sheet's default view of each type); stipple is the sheet's stipple knob at its default. bake_margin_px holds the wobble and line width inside the texture. A marker is baked once per type, side and scale and re-baked only when the host's scale drifts past rebake_ratio either way (a zoom), never per frame; min/max_bake_ppm bound the bake. cache_max (proposed 2026-10-09, fix pass) bounds the cache of baked arts, least recently used out first: three silhouettes x two sides at a few scales each is a dozen entries, so 48 is room to spare and a zoom can no longer grow it without limit.
unit_art._variant_u3: PROPOSED by Track U3 (the strike, 2026-10-10): the anti-aircraft battery and the radio tower are drawn from the unit sheet's default view of each, as the planes and the tank are (the tank keeps its code default of 0). Their sheet indices (feeding the seed) are 4 and 6, scripts/ui/unit_marker_art.gd STATICS.

fonts._reason: The unit sheet's lettering stack (IM Fell English for names, its italic for specs), then system serifs; the first one installed is used. Sizes in px.

card._reason: The HUD cards float above the map (design doc, UI and HUD: 'UI that looks like it floats above the game'): a cream card with the sheet's double neatline, casting a shadow in the map's own shadow tint and strength, offset lift_px away from the sun (the map's sun_direction). Sizes in px.

roster._reason: Right-hand sidebar summarising the units the players control (design doc, Unit roster sidebar). One row per player-controlled unit: side mark, name, type, speed, altitude band, plan status as pips (steps planned of steps per turn). Sorting and grouping come later: the row list goes through one function (roster.gd ordered_ids) so a sort is a change there. Sizes in px.
roster._reason_u2: PROPOSED by Track U2 (the first fight, 2026-10-09). A row grew to three lines (row_px 50 -> 62): name and health pips; type, speed and band; the plan status. The status echoes the map: a solid short path ending in a dot for 'has a plan', a dashed one ending in an open circle for 'no plan (flies on)', the same marks the planner draws, with the step pips (steps planned of steps per turn) at the right. A down unit's row is greyed (role row_down) with its name struck through and the state in place of the plan. The header counts the units that still need orders while the turn is being planned (design doc: 'a needs orders view helps co-op players split up the work'); with group-by 'none' (the default) the row order never changes; with 'needs orders' rows sit under headings and move only by the rule in roster.group._reason.

bombs._reason: PROPOSED by Track U3 (the strike, 2026-10-10; design doc UI table: a roster row carries 'special readiness'). A unit with bombs (World.bombs_left) shows its bomb load at the right of the row's second line: one small bomb mark per DROP the type carries, filled for a drop still to make and an outline for one spent, then 'x n' for the bombs in each drop (Alex: 'multiple passes make sense'; smaller bombers carry fewer, both per drop and in drops). Ink only. Like the health pips, the drops shown during a playback are the ones the unit had when the turn began, and one empties as its bomb_release event passes: a resolve does not spoil a release the player has not seen. Only the players' own units are listed, so an enemy's load is never shown. Sizes in px.

group._reason: PROPOSED by Track U2 (Alex 2026-10-09: 'we want a group by for needs orders'). A group-by control in the roster header (a button that cycles the modes) puts the rows under small headings, so co-op players can split up the work. Built modes: 'none' (the world's order, no headings; the default, proposed) and 'needs_orders' (headings needs orders / planned / down). The doc's other groupings (domain, unit type, nest) are not built: a mode is an entry in 'modes' and a branch in roster.gd _group_key. The choice is a per-player VIEW setting kept in the Roster, never in the World and never sent over the network. THE RULE THAT KEEPS A ROW STILL (proposed): the grouped layout is recomputed at once when planning starts, when the mode changes and when units are added or removed; at any other change (an edit by this or another player) it is recomputed only while the pointer is NOT over the roster, and the row of the SELECTED unit keeps the group it was in until another unit is selected. While the pointer is over the roster nothing moves; the roster catches up when the pointer leaves. During the playback the layout is held. Sizes in px.
group.label: group by

health._reason: PROPOSED by Track U2. Health (design doc, UI table, proposed treatment): segmented pips on the unit's row, echoed as a short arc on the selection ring. A unit has def.health pips (Unit.health left); the lost ones are drawn as empty outlines, so a row always shows the unit's full size. Pips are ink and outline only (palette rule: hue is reserved for paper, ink, shadow and the side accents; material is linework). Segments narrow to fit max_w_px when a type has many. The ring arc is one arc of segments on the selection ring's side that is clear of the side badge and the leader line, outside the ring's ticks (drawn by scripts/ui/health_arc.gd on UnitUI's overlay layer, so the marker layer is untouched). Sizes in px / degrees.

orders._reason: The motion-planning card under the roster: the selected unit's next step, an altitude control for the step just placed (dive / level / climb, one band per step as the units' bands_per_step allows), undo the last step, clear the plan, and the turn's Ready (commit for the local player; pressing it again withdraws). Sizes in px.
orders._u3: PROPOSED by Track U3 (the strike): the Drop control joins Dive / Level / Climb as a fourth button of the first row (Alex: bombing is 'per step, just like diving'), disabled for a unit with no bombs or none left; under that row a line (drop_line_px, kept for every unit so the card never changes size) says what the Drop control does for the step it acts on: the spread and the release of a drop planned, or why there is none. height_px grew 238 -> 258 for it.

marker._reason: Something on screen for every unit (exit criterion 6): the plane in ink at true scale, its shadow away from the sun by its drawn height (Alex: the gap is the altitude cue), a side mark (a small roundel in the side accent tied to the plane by a short leader), and for the selected unit an inked double ring, with a leader line up to its roster row; during a resolve's playback each unit trails the track it has flown (solid) and the rest of its turn (dashed) (design doc, UI and HUD: 'an inked ring drawn around the unit on the map, with a leader line up to its floating panel'). Sizes in px unless named _m.
marker._static_scale: PROPOSED by Track U3 (the strike, 2026-10-10): a STATIC unit (the radio tower, an anti-aircraft battery) is drawn static_scale times the plane rule (true_scale) -- 'at their own scale', as the planes are. Why 2: the planes are drawn up to twice their true size so they stay findable when zoomed out (data/scenarios sandbox view.plane_px, plane_min_px), while a tower 6 m across is 4 px at the planning zoom and the TARGET must read there; 2 puts the tower about as wide as a house and a battery about a house's width. 1.0 is the plain rule. The unit's cast shadow scales with it (it is baked with the art), so the tower's long shadow is always its height x the sun's length at the drawn scale.

ahead_line._reason: PROPOSED by Track U2 (combat on screen): the dashed line the marker layer draws ahead of a plane during a playback, the rest of the turn it is about to fly. applies_to 'own' draws it for the players' own planes only (Alex: the enemy's plans are never shown, and the rest of an enemy's turn is its plan; 'all' is what it was). Whatever the setting, a unit that goes down this turn has the line only up to the moment it goes down, and a unit already down has none: a fall, a blast, a phantom path beyond it would spoil the death before it is seen, as the pips are held back so that a hit is not.

trails._reason: WINGTIP TRAILS (Alex 2026-10-10: 'For locating the players planes, what about wingtip trails in the players color? That cover the past turn.'). The board is variants/wingtip-trails/; EVERY VALUE HERE IS PROPOSED by Track U1 and nothing is chosen until Alex picks. mode: 'none' is today's look and the default (nothing is drawn); lines, steps, ribbon, rungs, wake are the board's options (see their blocks). Each wingtip's line starts AT the drawn wingtip (the wing outline's half-span, in the art's own metres, times the plane's drawn scale, so the two lines sit on the drawn wingtips at every zoom) and follows the unit's path over the last window_turns of play: the whole last resolved turn while planning, a rolling window behind the plane while a turn plays back. Drawn in the unit's side accent (side_a for the players, side_b for the enemy), fading from the plane to nothing at the far end. applies_to: 'own' = the player-controlled units only (Alex: 'the players planes'), 'all' = every unit in sight. Sizes in screen px. The trail is recorded from World history (World.sample at sample_s) when a turn is resolved, so it exists only for turns this client has seen resolve.
trails._decided: Alex 2026-10-10 on the board (decision 'wingtip-trails'): 'D · One ribbon between the wingtips' -- mode ribbon; '2 all moving units' -- applies_to all (every unit in sight through the fog, each in its own side colour); '5 yes' -- a plane falling OUT OF CONTROL keeps leaving its trail, the ribbon following the sampled fall path to the crash (an exploded unit's trail stops at down_at and a crashed one's at the crash, then fades as the window rolls on); and 'the trail is to the current position' -- the ribbon runs right up to the plane, now (the end of the last turn while planning, the playback clock while a turn plays), and the whole-flight line stops where the ribbon starts (WingtipTrails.start_t). Still proposed: a one-turn window and the overlap with the cone wash.
trails._under_smoke: PROPOSED by Track U2 (2026-10-10), on the effects track's finding: Alex chose the smoke W1, soft white to grey, and the ribbon in the side colour, drawn over white smoke along the same centre line, nearly hides it. true = the ribbon is drawn UNDER the effects layer (ribbon, then ground marks, shadows and smoke, then the planner and the cone wash, then the planes, then the bursts on top); false = the ribbon over the smoke, just under the planes, as it was mounted first. Alex has not ruled on this. UnitUI.apply_trail_order() reads it (setup() calls it; a host that changes the value at run time calls it again).
trails._replaces: While a trail mode other than none is on, the marker layer does not draw its own solid ink line of the track flown so far this turn during playback (the trail is that, at the wingtips); the dashed rest-of-turn line stays. The sandbox's whole-flight track (scripts/app/sandbox_tracks.gd, Track A's) is not touched by this switch: see the board's report for how it should stop at the last turn's start.

lines._about: Two thin solid lines, one per wingtip, fading to nothing over the window.

steps._about: The same, broken at each step's end so the steps read: a gap of gap_px at every step end (the planes' own step times).

ribbon._about: One soft band between the wingtips in the side colour, fading over the window, with a hairline along each edge.

rungs._about: Twin lines and a short rung across the wingtips at every step's end (the plane's own wing, left behind where each step ended).

wake._about: A tapered wake: the lines start at the wingtips and narrow and draw together toward the centre line as they age (converge 1 meets it at the end of the window), like a wake or a contrail, fading to nothing.

standout._reason: How the players' own units stand out on busy ground (Alex 2026-10-09: 'a comparison board for figuring out how to make your own units stand out visually on the busy background'; the heavy fighter is faint over trees). The board is variants/own-units-stand-out/; EVERY VALUE HERE IS PROPOSED by Track U1 and nothing is chosen until Alex picks. mode names ONE effect, or several joined with '+' (for example 'halo+ring'); 'none' is today's marker and the default, drawn exactly as before. The effects apply to the player-controlled units only (controller 'player': every co-op player's planes), never to the AI's. Colours are palette roles ({base, alpha, toward, t}, as in the roles block): hue stays reserved for paper, ink, shadow and the side accents, so the halo and the lift are PAPER, the rim is INK, the ring is the unit's own side accent. Sizes are screen px at the plane's drawn size.
standout._decided: Alex 2026-10-09 on the board: 'not quite there. Today's is the best' -- mode none (today's marker). The problem stays open for a later round.

halo._about: A paper knock-out round the silhouette, under the plane and its shadow (the map-label halo): the ground's ink is erased in a ring radius_px wide, feathered over soft_px more. Proposed.

lift._about: A soft paper lift under the plane: a pool of paper centred on the unit, full to inner_k x the plane's radius and gone at outer_k x. Proposed.

rim._about: A heavier outline on own units only: the silhouette grown by radius_px in ink, under the drawn outline. Proposed.

ring._about: A ring in the unit's own side accent under the plane, pad_px outside its silhouette radius, width_px wide, with an ink hairline (rim_role, rim_px) on its outer edge so it is inked like everything else. alpha is the accent's. Proposed.

larger._about: Own units drawn scale x larger than the rule says (a light fighter 36 px becomes 36 x scale); the shadow gap follows the drawn size. Proposed.

cones._reason: How the engagement cones are drawn on the map while planning (variants/cone-overlay/ is the board; EVERY VALUE AND RULE IS PROPOSED by Track U1 and nothing is chosen until Alex picks). mode: outline (an inked rim with range ticks, nothing inside), hatch (45 degree strokes in the side colour, more broken where the odds are lower), stipple (dots in the side colour, thinner where the odds are lower) or wash (a light wash in the side colour, in odds steps). The rim and a dot on every hardpoint are common to all four. Shading is the odds model's own centre factor (scripts/sim/combat.gd), so it is peaked for fixed guns and even for turrets and flexible guns. Colours are palette roles (hue only for the side accents); sizes are screen px, ranges true metres on the map.
cones._decided: Alex 2026-10-09 on the board: 'color wash (selected only)' -- mode wash; cones for the selected unit only, no enemy cones (the lead's reading of 'selected only'). Every other value here is still proposed.
cones._rules: own: 'selected' draws the selected player unit's cones, 'all_own' every player unit's. enemy: 'in_sight' draws an enemy unit's cones while that unit is visible through the fog, 'none' draws no enemy's. Proposed: own cones in the selected unit's planning view, enemy cones only while that enemy is in sight. Only while planning.
cones._overshoot: EFFECTIVE RANGE (Alex 2026-10-09: guns fire 'slightly over effective range'): a weapon's range_m is its effective range; past it the odds fall smoothly to 0 over a short overshoot. Track C builds the real factor (an overshoot of about 15 to 25% of the effective range, data/sim/combat.json); until the overlay's range_factor seam (scripts/ui/cone_overlay.gd) is pointed at it, THIS fraction (proposed 0.2, the middle of that band) and a smoothstep ramp stand in, so the falloff zone is drawn at the size the rule will have. falloff_side_alpha and falloff_dash_px: the wedge's sides carry on through the zone, dashed and fainter.
cones._label: Alex 2026-10-10 (decision side-view-look): no weapon labels on the cones, top-down or side view, for now -- they add noise; revisit when units carry many more hardpoints (perhaps a dropdown to pick the weapon). The lettering below stays for that day.

outline._about: An inked rim only, with ticks across the centre line every tick_every_m and a faint centre line.

hatch._about: 45 degree strokes spacing_px apart, in cells cell_px long; a cell is drawn with the probability of the odds there (a fixed gun's centre is solid, its rim is broken; a turret's is solid throughout).

stipple._about: Dots on a jittered grid cell_px square, a dot kept with the probability of the odds there to the power gamma.

wash._about: The side colour in `steps` bands from the centre line outwards for a peaked weapon, alpha_rim at the edge to alpha_centre in the middle; a flat weapon is one wash at alpha_flat.

planner._reason: The motion plan on the map (Alex: motion is a curve of steps; each step is a point inside the envelope; inertia applies). The next step's reachable region as an inked fan with ribs; the plan as an inked curve (planned steps solid, carry-on steps dashed) with a ghost of the unit at every step end; a clamped step shows a fine dashed tie from the point asked for to where the envelope put it. A press within capture_px of the fan starts a step; a press within handle_px of a planned step's end re-drags that step. Sizes in px.
planner._reason_u2: PROPOSED by Track U2. others_*: every OTHER player unit's plan stays on the map all the time during planning (co-op: everyone sees what has plans and what does not): thin and quiet, a solid line with a dot at each planned step's end, the carry-on rest dashed (a unit with no plan shows only the dashed flight, 'flies on'). others_alpha was 0.35 at the full path width; now 0.55 at about two thirds of it. speed_labels: the lettering at a planned step's ghost carries the speed the step ends at, 'n · 120 m/s' (unit: roster.speed_unit). An AI-controlled unit's plan is never drawn (motion_planner.gd plan_shown).

hover._reason: PROPOSED by Track U2 (Alex 2026-10-10: 'we also need a visual indicator for selecting path nodes; it is hard to tell when you are close enough'). Feedback for what a press here would do. As the pointer comes within near_factor x handle_px of a planned step's handle the handle shows (APPROACHING); inside handle_px (IN RANGE) it shows unmistakably that a press grabs THIS handle (the nearest one: crowded handles go to the closest); the highlight stays while the step is dragged. The mouse cursor follows (cursor.*): a pointing hand over a grabbable handle, a grabbing hand while dragging, a cross where a press would place the next step (the fan and its capture_px), the arrow otherwise; it is reset when the pointer leaves, the plan closes or the unit cannot take orders. mode is one or more effects joined with '+': grow (the handle's dot grows and fills), ring (a ring round the handle that closes in on the pointer's distance and locks at handle_px, where a second rule joins it), halo (a paper pool behind the handle that erases the busy ground), magnet (a line from the pointer to the handle), label (the step's lettering gets a paper plate and full ink). Every effect is ink, paper or the unit's own side accent (palette rule 6). The board variants/node-hover/ shows the options at four pointer states and two zooms; the default here is the recommended one, PROPOSED, nothing is chosen. handle_px (the pick radius) was 12 and is 16 PROPOSED: a 24 px target is the least a mouse needs and is small for a trackpad or a finger; with the nearest handle winning, a bigger radius no longer costs the neighbour step anything, and the ring now SHOWS the radius; 16 px still clears the next step's fan at the start zoom (its near edge is 31 px from the last handle at minimum speed). Sizes in px.
hover._decided: Alex 2026-10-10 on the board: 'A · Grow and fill' -- mode grow. Still proposed: the 16 px pick radius (was 12), the cursor changes, the place mark.

labels._reason: HEIGHT AND SPEED LABELS (Track U3, 2026-10-10; Alex: height is hard to read from above -- 'make sure that every unit and every node has a height and speed label'). EVERY VALUE HERE IS PROPOSED by Track U3; the lead proposed the compact format. EVERY unit marker the map shows (a player's, an enemy's, whenever the unit is in sight) carries one small inked label under it, its CURRENT height in metres and speed (live through a playback: the pose the marker is drawn at); a STATIC unit (the radio tower, a battery) has its height above the ground (0 m) and no speed. EVERY plan node carries one too: a planned step's lettering is 'n . speed m/s . height m' (the height folded into the existing line), and a carry-on step, which had none, 'speed m/s . height m' (fainter). Never anything about an enemy's PLAN (its nodes are not drawn at all: motion_planner.gd plan_shown); an enemy's current state is visible state. Ink at moderate alpha with the paper under-stroke the hover uses, so the label reads over the grove.
labels._height_ref: PROPOSED: what the height means. 'sim' (the default) is the height the SIMULATION flies and bombs by (the altitude band's metres, between two bands during a band change; data/sim/altitude.json): the number the bomb's fall time, throw and spread are computed from, so a player aiming a drop reads the figure that decides it. 'ground' is the height above the terrain under the unit (what the shadow gap shows; Track T's height_at), the same figure where the ground is 0 and a smaller one over a ridge. Alex has not said.
labels._unit: A mobile unit: height in metres, then speed in m/s with the unit left off (the roster beside it says m/s).
labels._hide: PROPOSED far-zoom rule: labels hide when the map's scale falls under this many screen px per metre (the planning zoom 0.35 at 2 px/m is 0.7 and shows them; 0.5 is zoom 0.25), below which units are a few px apart and a line of lettering each is noise. The far overview (fog-first-option) hides them all.
labels._below: px between the selection ring's outer ticks and the unit label's top edge.

target._reason: THE TARGET SELECTION ON THE MAP (Track T, 2026-10-10). In force (Alex, decision special-targeting): 'when you have a friendly unit selected, you can also select either an enemy unit or a point on the map'; set by 'left-click an enemy unit, right-click a point on the map -- fine for now. Right click drag is awkward so we will change later' (right-drag still pans: a right press and release without movement is the click). EVERYTHING HERE IS PROPOSED by Track T: the marks (ink, with a paper pool under them, on the map's own palette roles -- hue stays reserved for paper, ink, shadow and the side accents), their sizes (screen px, so they read at the planning zoom 0.35 and at zoom 1), and the two slops.
target._slops: right_click.slop_px: a right press and release that moves no farther than this (screen px) is a click and sets a point target; farther it was a pan, which the camera has already taken. aim_drag_slop_px: dragging a step's aim handle moves the step's target (it becomes a point) only once the pointer has moved this far (screen px) from where the handle was grabbed, so a plain click on an aim that sits on a unit does not nudge it.

unit._about: A unit target: four corner brackets round the unit's marker, half a side = the marker's radius + pad_px, never less than min_half_px.

point._about: A point target: a diamond with a dot, r_px from the centre to a corner.

quiet._about: The target of another step, or of another player's drop: the same marks, smaller and fainter.

blocked._about: A drop whose target is outside its cone (it will not release, or is a poor shot): a slash across the aim's mark, and the word beside it.

bombs._reason: THE BOMB DROP IN THE INTERFACE (Track U3, the strike, 2026-10-10). In force (Alex 2026-10-10, decisions bomb-release and bomb-load): a drop is 'per step, just like diving. You set the intent in the cone. The accuracy is based on how close you are to the ideal release angle', height is a factor, and a bomber makes several drops ('multiple passes make sense'; smaller bombers carry fewer, per drop and in drops). So: the orders card's Drop control turns a drop on for the step it acts on (the last placed step, or the step whose handle was grabbed last); with it on, the map shows that step's BOMB CONE (World.drop_cone: where this step's release can put the bombs) and the player places the AIM POINT in it, a handle like a step's with the same grow-and-fill hover (Alex's node-hover pick); the planner shows the expected spread at the aim and how close the release is to ideal. EVERY VALUE HERE IS PROPOSED by Track U3; nothing is chosen. The enemy's drops are never shown (the one rule is motion_planner.gd plan_shown).

text._about: The orders card's words for the Drop control (orders.drop_line_px) and the lettering at a step with a drop.
text.label: Drop
text.none_left: drop: no drops left to plan
text.free: drops free: %d of %d, %d bombs a drop
text._target: Track T, 2026-10-10, PROPOSED wording (Alex, special-targeting: no target, no activation; a target outside the step's cone, the special cannot be activated on that step and the card says why). The lines are kept under ~40 characters: the card's line is 258 px of 12 px italic. wont_release / poor_shot are the two ways a drop already set can have its target outside the cone (a step moved after it was set; a followed unit leaving the cone): data/sim/bombs.json outside_cone_mode picks which one the card and the map word.
text.no_target: no target: click an enemy, or right-click
text.wont_release: will not release: target outside the cone
text.poor_shot: poor shot: target outside the cone
text._expected: The expected-damage line (bombs.aoe.card_line): the most affected ground unit in sight, from the sim's own rules (World.drop_expected). %s the unit, %s its expected pips (one decimal when under 10, else whole), %d its health, %d the accuracy percent.

aim._reason: How the bomb cone and the aim mark with its spread are drawn (variants/bomb-aim/ is the board; EVERY VALUE AND RULE IS PROPOSED by Track U3 and nothing is chosen until Alex picks). mode: outline (an inked rim, a dotted fall line and a dashed spread ellipse), wash (the cone as a wash in the side colour, deeper toward the ideal aim, a crosshair and a faint inked spread ellipse: the cone wash Alex chose for guns, used for bombs), stipple (the cone in dots, thinner away from the ideal aim, and the spread as a scatter of dots: where bombs may land) or rings (range rings from the release point through the cone, the aim ring solid). The rim, the crosshair and the ideal mark are common to all four. Colours are palette roles (hue only for the side accent): the interior is the unit's side accent, everything else is ink or paper. Sizes are screen px; distances true metres on the map.

preview._about: Track T, PROPOSED: while a target is set and the step the card is about has no drop yet, the step's bomb cone is drawn faintly (a wash at this alpha of the side colour and a dashed rim) so the player sees where the target has to be -- the card says why Drop is off, the map says where the cone is. Switched off by preview_cone false.

aim._decided: not yet: variants/bomb-aim/board.json has chosen: null. The mode above is the lead-in recommendation of the board, PROPOSED, so the build gives feedback before Alex picks.

spread._about: The ellipse that holds most of the drop's stick: sigma_k times the sim's one-bomb scatter (a standard deviation: 2 holds 86 percent of a round scatter), longer along the bomber's heading by half the stick (the bombs of a drop land a few metres apart along it).

quiet._about: The aim of a step that is not the one the card is about, and another player's drop: a small mark, no cone.

wash._about: The side colour in `steps` nested copies of the cone, each shrunk toward the ideal aim (to shrink_to of its size at the last), alpha_rim at the edge to alpha_centre at the ideal aim: the more of it, the closer the release is to ideal.

stipple._about: Dots on a jittered grid cell_px square in the cone, kept with the probability of closeness to the ideal aim to the power gamma; the spread is scatter_dots impacts scattered as the expected spread says (a fixed pattern, seeded from the unit and the step, so it does not shimmer).

rings._about: Arcs about the release point at every ring_every_m of range inside the cone, dashed and faint, and the aim's own ring solid.

aoe._reason: THE AREA OF EFFECT of a bomb drop on the map (Track T, 2026-10-10; variants/bomb-aoe/ is the board). Alex: 'For bombs, I expected area of effect as well.' How it is drawn is a BOARD decision and nothing is chosen: the mode below is a WORKING DEFAULT, PROPOSED so the build gives feedback before Alex picks. none: nothing. rings: the blast table's rings (12, 25 and 45 m: 3, 2 and 1 pips) round the aim, on top of the scatter. footprint: ONE wash, the scatter grown by the blast's reach ('anything in here takes damage'). impacts: the stick's bombs along the track, each with its own blast circle. tiers (proposed by Track T as a fourth option): the scatter grown by each blast tier, three nested washes, darker toward more pips. Every mode is drawn from the sim's own numbers (the blast table in data/sim/bombs.json, the scatter and the stick the aim gets); the lines are ink on the map's paper (hue stays reserved for paper, ink, shadow and the side accents -- the cone beside it is the side accent, the area of effect is not a second hue), so lightness is the ramp: darker is more damage. card_line: the orders card's line names the unit in sight that is expected to lose the most pips ('radio tower: about 5 of 8'), computed from the sim's own rules (World.drop_expected).
aoe._decided: not yet: variants/bomb-aoe/board.json has chosen: null
aoe._card_min_pips: The orders card's line names a unit that is NOT the step's unit target only when it is expected to lose at least this many pips (a battery that loses 0.04 pips is not worth a line); the unit target itself is always named.

rings._about: The blast table's rings round the lands point: the 3-pip ring solid, the others dashed, each numbered with its pips when label_px is above 0 and the ring is wide enough to read.

footprint._about: One wash, the scatter's ellipse grown by the farthest blast tier, with an inked edge.

impacts._about: The stick's bombs at their nominal places along the bomber's heading, centred on the aim: a dot, the direct-hit ring solid and the farthest reach faint.

tiers._about: The scatter grown by each blast tier, outermost first: each wash adds its alpha, so the nearest tier (the most pips) is the darkest. The outer edge is dashed, the 3-pip edge solid.

side_view._reason: THE SIDE VIEW (Track V, 2026-10-10; scripts/ui/side_view.gd and side_view_art.gd). In force (Alex, decisions height-speed-labels and side-view-look): 'a side view indicator that only shows the firing cone and the relative straight line position of the targeted enemy'; 'for the side view I like the color wash. Keep the style identical to the top down. Reduce the icons (plane, tower, etc) to just indicators. I don't want side view assets'; 'remove the weapon labels on the graph'. And (special-targeting): the target is an enemy unit or a map point, shown here, and a special's own step keeps its target. And (2026-10-10, his word on moving targets): a unit target follows the unit, drawn at its SHOWN position, and the bombs' release point is picked dynamically. EVERYTHING ELSE HERE IS PROPOSED by Track V: where it sits (the bottom of the orders card, the mock-up's place; the card grows by the section while the panel shows), its size and the scale rule (one scale on both axes, so every angle is true; the span from the weapons' reach, a target beyond it an arrow on the edge), the marks (a dot, a cross, a tick), and the one quiet line of text. The cones are drawn by cone_overlay.gd's own functions from the weapons' own data, so the wash, its odds shading toward the centre for fixed guns and its fade past the effective range are the map's. Colours are palette roles (hue only for the side accents). Sizes in px unless named _m.
side_view._cone_mode: Alex chose the colour wash for the side view (decision side-view-look); the map's own mode (planner.cones.mode) is a separate switch, so the two can differ.
side_view._live: PROPOSED: while a turn plays back the panel stays up for the selected friendly unit at its SHOWN pose, with the selection's target drawn at ITS shown position, so a moving target is followed (Alex: 'Targeting a moving unit like a tank should follow the unit'). The picture is the shown positions, never a prediction: nothing of an enemy's plan is read. false hides the panel from the moment the turn resolves.

section._about: The section at the bottom of the orders card: a faint rule, a line saying which step, the picture, the quiet line. gap_px is the room under the card's own content. The picture shrinks to fit the window (the card must stay on screen) and the whole section is left out under min_picture_h_px.

frame._about: The metres-to-px rule. ONE scale for both axes. Guns view: the horizontal span is the longest reach (effective range plus the fade) of the weapons that face forward, times span_margin, and of those that face rearward on the left (the room behind a unit with none is rear_room_fraction of the forward span); at least span_min_m. The unit sits down the page where its cones need room (their extents above and below it, the ground when near; unit_y_frac when they need none), between unit_y_min_frac and unit_y_max_frac of the height, and moved as far as the page allows to give a target on the page the room it needs. A target the picture does not hold is an arrow on the edge, edge_inset_px in.

mark._about: The selected plane: a small mark in its side's accent (the roundel's colour) with an ink rim, and a pitch tick, a short ink stroke along the nose, tilted by the step's pitch (combat.json max_pitch_deg, the same tilt the cones take).

target._about: The target: an enemy plane a dot in its side's accent with an ink rim; a ground unit (the tower, a battery) a tick standing on the ground line; a map point a small ink cross; beyond the picture an arrow on the edge pointing at it. off_axis_hollow (PROPOSED): the picture is the vertical plane along the unit's nose and cannot show a bearing, so a plane dot whose bearing is wider than every gun's arc that faces its way is drawn as a ring instead of a dot (it is in the picture, not in a gun's arc).

drop._about: A step with a drop shows the bombs' fall instead of the cones: the bomber at its release, the arc the stick falls (bombs.gd's own bomb_position: level across, height 1 - f^2), where it lands (the aim, as drop_spread clamps it into the cone) with the expected spread on the ground, and the target on the ground line. The scale fits the fall: the width to the landing and the spread (and the target), the height from the release to the ground, margins top_px / bottom_px / left_px / right_px.
drop._fit: PROPOSED: the scale makes room for the target as well as the fall, up to this many times the fall's own span (the landing and its spread); a target farther than that is an arrow on the edge, so a stray target cannot shrink the fall to nothing.
drop._unreleased: PROPOSED: a drop the sim would NOT release (its target is outside the step's cone and data/sim/bombs.json outside_cone_mode is 'hold'; the orders card says why) is drawn at this fraction of the arc's and the spread's alpha, the arc still going to the cone's nearest point (what drop_spread reports as the aim).

text._about: The words. enabled false drops the quiet line under the picture (the weapon labels are not here: Alex took them off the graph as noise). PROPOSED default: on, because the picture shows the angle and the line gives the two numbers that make it exact (the slant distance and the height difference), a single line of soft italic.

combat._reason: COMBAT ON SCREEN (Track U2, the first fight, part 2, 2026-10-10). EVERY VALUE HERE IS PROPOSED by Track U2; none is a decision. In force (Alex): a downed plane either explodes mid air or goes out of control and crashes eventually; a crash is an explosion, then a smoking wreck; particles are fast flashes with a very slow decay; no fire for now, just smoke (so everything drawn here is ink and paper); the enemy's plans are never shown; the design doc's damage rule: 'a brief ink mark on the unit when hit, following the fast-flash, slow-decay rule; pips drop on the card'. Times are game seconds (a turn is 5), sizes px unless named _m.

fall._about: A plane falling out of control (marker layer): its marker keeps flying the sim's sampled path with its shadow gap closing as the sim's fall height drops, and it rocks: a wobble of wobble_deg either side of its heading at wobble_hz (the phase is the game clock and the unit's id, so planes do not rock together), eased in over ramp_s after it goes down, plus a slow spin of spin_dps (0 = none). The sim already spirals it at fall_turn_rate_dps (data/sim/combat.json), so the rock is slight. An exploded plane's marker is gone from down_at and a crashed one's at the crash; neither has a plan drawn.

hit_mark._about: The brief ink mark on a unit when it is hit (a 'hit' event as the playback clock passes it). FAST FLASH, VERY SLOW DECAY: at once, a flash of paper (a pool that knocks the busy ground out, gone in flash_s) with the ink burst on it at full strength; the ink then fades over life_s along (1 - age / life_s) ^ decay_power. A burst of rays short strokes round a dot, wobbled by hand, sized radius_k x the plane's drawn radius (not under min_radius_px or over max_radius_px; a hit that took more pips than one is damage_k bigger per extra pip), set spot_k of the plane's radius off its centre in a direction picked by the hit (the unit's id and the event's time), in the plane's own frame so it rides with the plane. Ink and paper only. The mark's clock is the playback's while a turn plays; when the turn is over it carries on in real time (at the playback speed) until it is gone, and a new turn clears what is left. A unit that is not drawn (fog, or exploded at that moment) shows none.

tracers._about: A faint streak for each shot (a 'fire' event, one per roll), from the muzzle to the target (a miss carries on past it by miss_overshoot_k of the distance, off the line by the roll's own miss). OFF BY DEFAULT (proposed): a dogfight rolls dozens of shots a turn, so streaks would bury the map in lines that only echo what the hit marks, the pips and the cone wash already say, and a shot is a roll against the odds, not a bullet that was aimed. The switch is here for Alex to look at.

fx._about: The effects layer (scripts/fx/fx_layer.gd, Track X) as UnitUI mounts it. select_smoke / select_crash: the options to run, '' = fx.json's working defaults (the smoke is Alex's W1, decision damage-smoke; fire is off, decision fire-colour; the crash option is still open). select_crash_smoke: the smoke a crash draws (a falling plane's trail, the burst's cloud, the wreck's column); '' = the same as the damage smoke, so the game has one smoke (PROPOSED by the lead). restore_age_s: a wreck put back by a client that joined late (or after a rebuild) is given the age this many game seconds, so it is already a settled scar and its embers are long out. smoke_when_hidden: false = a unit outside the player's sight leaves no smoke and no blast on the map (a trail of puffs would give away where it flew); a crash out of sight still puts its scar down quietly.

result._about: The end-of-mission card (UnitUI.show_result with Mission.evaluate()'s shape {state, reason, turn, t}): a veil over the map and the sidebar, a card in the UI's style with the verdict, the reason in plain words and two buttons. reasons turns the mission's own reason string into words: the first pattern (a regular expression) that matches wins, and %s in its text is the display name of the unit the pattern captured in lower case ('bomber'; the captured text itself if it is not a unit of the world). No pattern matching shows the mission's own words. Planning input is locked while it shows. Sizes in px.

text.won_title: V I C T O R Y
text.lost_title: D E F E A T

reasons.text: the tower still stands after turn %s

roles._reason: Every colour the interface draws, as a palette role. Cards are the object fill (cream) on the paper map; text and rules are the ink at the sheet's alpha steps; the selected row is the paper itself showing through; the fan is a faint ink wash; shadows are the map's shadow tint at the map's shadow strength.

keys._reason: Keyboard shortcuts for the planner, by Godot key name.
keys._clear_target: Track T, PROPOSED: Esc clears the target selection before it clears anything else (and before it leaves to the menu).

shot._reason: scripts/ui/ui_shot.gd only. The map scale is an open question for Alex; 3.8 px/m is the PLACEHOLDER proposed today (the unit sheet's true-scale strip, where the prototype's 38 px canopy is a ~10 m tree). Nothing outside the shot reads it: every UI piece takes its mapping from its host.
